subject: MAP deliverables: evaluation metrics briefcase & exec readout

From: Alice Porter <alice@acme-corp.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Cho <ben.cho@acme-corp.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: MAP metrics and exec slides

Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — Acme's procurement and infra teams want a short, verifiable performance bundle we can include in the MAP. Specifically they're asking for:
- Latency (p50/p90/p99) for our recommended model at target prompts (2 prompt lengths)
- Throughput (tokens/sec) and TTFT (time-to-first-token) by concurrency (1, 4, 16)
- A CSV export with raw measurement rows (timestamp, model, seq_len, concurrency, ttft_ms, p50_ms, p90_ms, p99_ms, tokens_per_sec)
- A one-page executive slide summarizing risk/fit for production and a link to an interactive dashboard

Can you confirm what you can deliver and a timeline? We need the bundle to attach to the MAP by COB next Tuesday (2026-11-24) to keep the procurement review on schedule.

Also helpful if you can include any known fallback suggestions (model variants / quant profiles) that preserve latency under 95th percentile SLOs.

Appreciate it —
Alice
Alice Porter
Senior Infra PM, Acme Cyber
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Request: MAP metrics and exec slides

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear ask. Below is the delivery plan we propose; happy to compress timelines if you need earlier artifacts.

Planned deliverables (MAP briefcase):
1) Raw CSV export (format you described) — draft by today 11/20 15:00 PT, final by 11/23 12:00 PT
2) Executive readout slide (one slide + supporting appendix slides) — initial PDF by 11/20 15:00 PT
3) Interactive dashboard link + query notes (Datadog/Grafana) — shared 11/20 15:00 PT; refreshed exports 11/23
4) Short mitigation notes: recommended model variants + quantization profiles for cost vs latency tradeoffs

Quick snapshot of scope we will measure: two prompt lengths (32 tokens, 256 tokens), model variant A (default) and variant B (quant 4-bit), concurrency sweep 1 / 4 / 16, 100 steady-state iterations per config, TTFT measured at connection cold/warm.

I will own the external delivery. Internally Marissa will normalize the CSV columns and Jordan will author the executive slide.

Can you confirm a 30-minute exec readout window on Mon 11/23 at 11:00 PT? If confirmed we'll schedule a calendar invite.

Deliverables will be attached to this thread (drive + CSV stub) once Marissa/Jordan finish the assemble.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: ACME MAP briefcase: attached CSVs, slides, and dashboard links

Alice / Ben — attaching the ACME briefcase as discussed. Quick summary of what's included below; attachments and Drive links at the bottom.

What we included:
- acme_metrics_raw.csv: raw measurement rows (columns: ts_iso, model, variant, seq_len, concurrency, ttft_ms, p50_ms, p90_ms, p99_ms, tokens_per_sec)
- acme_map_toc.csv: short TOC for the briefcase (what each file is and how to interpret)
- acme_exec_readout_slides_v1.pdf: 1-page executive summary + 2 appendix slides (latency curves by prompt length and concurrency table)
- Dashboard: live view of the runs with filters for seq_len and concurrency; queries are linked in the appendix

Key takeaways for MAP:
- Default model variant meets p90 < 200ms for short prompts at concurrency <=4; p99 spikes at 16 under synthetic peak load (recommend canary with quant-4 variant to reduce 95th percentile by ~30%)
- TTFT cold vs warm: cold median ~120ms, warm median ~22ms — included in CSV and appendix
- Suggested MAP language: include the CSV + readout slide as the performance appendix; call out model variant and suggested fallback policy for peak-hour service.

Attachments (stubs):
- acme_metrics_raw.csv (CSV)
- acme_map_toc.csv (CSV)
- acme_exec_readout_slides_v1.pdf (PDF)

Drive & tracking links:

- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/ACME-2026-Q4-42
- Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.com/d/ACME-eval?orgId=1

I've scheduled the 30-minute exec readout for Mon, 2026-11-23 11:00 PT (calendar invite sent). If you'd like a dry run before the readout we can do a 15-minute prep Friday afternoon.

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
